utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. We will hear first the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian and Ann Sutherland assisted by Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Mr. Branko Lukic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is Mr. Ostojic coming back?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are expecting him, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Just before we start with today's witness, we just in the courtroom received numerous documents. It's never too late. But for tomorrow, it's really poor what we have. It's two lines and one sentence. Is there anything additional for Witness 59?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's some additional material coming at the break. It will be ready at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The break today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Today, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I heard that there was an appointment between Judge Lindholm and the Defence to review the documents on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 11.00 a.m., Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So the there would be no further obstacle for starting the exercise with the forensic handwriting expert. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Actually, there is an obstacle which I would like to address the Court about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Obviously, we're anxious to get those documents as soon as possible. And also I would request if documents are excluded, since this is an ex parte hearing, that at least the Prosecution gets some notice of the general nature of the documents that were excluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If any. Regarding the two experts that Your Honours requested, because both experts will be dealing with documents that overlap, there's a problem about who we give those original documents to. We've not yet identified a -- the handwriting expert. We have identified a potential expert regarding the document analysis. Those experts were contacted today, and I'm awaiting a fax from them, but I have been told from my investigator that they told him I believe this morning that they could not complete their report by the 26th of August, and that they would need the physical custody of the documents for quite some period of time. I'm not sure of the exact period of time. Those same documents would have to go to the handwriting expert. It was just my initial reaction, which I wanted to confirm with Your Honours, that the handwriting expert would get priority and that Your Honours would prefer the documents first go to the handwriting expert rather than the document examiner to compare the machines in which they were printed on. And there would be a -- it is a smaller set regarding the handwriting, since the handwriting originals only include those that we believe were signed by Dr. Stakic. As I understood Your Honours' request, the document examiner really was going to compare those to also originals that are only typed with no signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right, indeed, there was a -- how can I call it -- hidden hope, that the expert would have the expertise for both exercises. But if not, priority has to be given without any doubt to the handwriting expert. Probably the other expert, if two experts are needed, could start on the basis of the documents where no such signature can be found, and then transfer the other documents to the second expert. To emphasise, if two experts are really needed. But as you just heard, the new additional material, handwriting material, will be ready by Wednesday. And as far as I have heard, it's only very, very limited. And so there is a likelihood that you'll receive it on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We're having some trouble with one of the potential experts that we had, although the person had some background in former Yugoslavia, did not feel comfortable making any comparisons with Cyrillic. Also the lab we contacted regarding the documentation said they would not feel comfortable. It was a western country's crime lab, dealing with documents in Cyrillic. We are attempting to contact one country where Cyrillic is the principal alphabet, but so far we have not been able to get a commitment from them that they would be able to do it. And it is looking difficult to get that commitment. And I'm not sure how they would deal with the Latin. They may have the same problem dealing with Latin. I'm not sure. But we're working on those, just to alert Your Honours to those issues. Also, when Your Honours would like, I'd like to address the schedule for the next two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. We would appreciate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For this week, Your Honour, we have two witnesses. The present witness we anticipated would take up to two days, but Ms. Sutherland who proofed him thinks it may be shorter. He is apparently very direct in answering questions. The next witness is Witness Number 59, is Mr. Mayhew, and he will be arriving tomorrow night and he will testify on Wednesday. For the following week, we have two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, isn't there a Thursday in this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: He will be more than one day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In anticipation. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think we estimate him at one and a half or two days. For the following week, there was -- there are two witnesses that we had -- I mentioned this last week. Two witnesses that we had anticipated calling this month, crime-based witnesses, who now it appears we will not be able to call, because they refuse to come, basically. One has medical problems and the other is refusing to respond, but also, according to the spouse of that person, has medical problems. In order to replace those, both of them, I believe, talk about the Benkovac barracks, or one of them does. The Benkovac barracks killings, one of the charged killings. We previously put in an application for Witness Number 42 to testify via 92 bis. We would like to call that witness live next week. We've actually arranged that with the witness tentatively. So the witness would be here Monday to testify, because that would then be the live witness for that killing, and we will not have any other live witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That would be the former witness number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 42. We also anticipate as I mentioned last week --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And this witness, sorry to interrupt, for one day or for two days?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think one and a half would be a rough estimate. We anticipated, as I mentioned last week, the demographer, Ms. Tabeau testifying, simply regarding part of her report that was disclosed, that is, the demographic changes, without going into the sections on the number of people missing and killed, because that is -- data is two years old and she is in the process of updating that with newly available data. And that report, however, will not be ready until, probably, the beginning of August. So we anticipate that she would have to testify again in September regarding that part, an updated report regarding the persons who were killed or missing and the socioeconomic status of those persons. We could call next week Mr. Inayat, because we're running out of -- we simply don't anticipate that those two witnesses will take the whole week. We may even finish those in two days, two or three days. So Mr. Inayat will be available along with a very - we have some - I finished going through all of the -- almost all of the documents on our original 65 ter list, actually all of those, there are some new ones that have been added. And we will put in our list 6 which will hopefully include all of the documents that we will submit in the case. There may be a few miscellaneous ones that will come in through the witnesses. But that list 6 should be ready, and we could call Mr. Inayat to testify regarding the sources of all the documents that have been admitted so far. Just so Your Honours know, Mr. Mayhew, the next witness after the one today, I have been told has cancelled a seminar to be here this week. He has been very cooperative in trying to fit our schedule, his schedule to our schedule. And Ms. Sutherland would like to address you regarding the protective measures for the witness who will testify today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we first ask the Defence, are there any observations to be made on the plannings for the next two weeks, especially, will Mr. Ostojic be present when we may hear once again Mr. Inayat?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic will be present, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any other additional problems or observations from your side?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic will cross-examine Mr. Mayhew as well, so we really need him in this courtroom and hopefully he will be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we start with the preparation, first, of our next witness, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I wish to make an application, oral application, that the next witness be heard in closed session. The witness was originally granted a pseudonym with image and voice distortion; however, on speaking with the witness yesterday and going over areas of proposed testimony, it will mean that there are a large number of areas where we would need to go into private session. And it would mean jumping in and out constantly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't think that you have to give additional reasons. When discussing the issue this morning, I already wondered why only these protective measures and why not closed session. Any objections against closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we never object to any kind of protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I thought the same thing as I was reviewing the statement, but the Prosecution, and the Defence I think also, would want to hear as much evidence as possible in open session, and we thought we were trying to do the right thing. But it's just going to be impossible, I think. And it would flow much more freely if it was in closed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good to know -- we'll proceed this way. But I forgot one issue,and this was related to a 92 bis statement with (redacted) (redacted). We first wanted to hear this person as a live witness. Then we compromised, videolink, to do it with the assistance of a videolink. And then finally, having heard the arguments, we agreed that 92 bis would be sufficient. But I heard that there would be additional obstacles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, this is Witness number 60 -- sorry, 1-6, 16. If Your Honour could redact the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please. The witness name may be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we applied to the registry for an officer to go take that statement, and apparently there is a problem in coordinating with the registry and a time when that can take place. The witness, according to the information I received, rather difficult in some ways, and is elderly. There's one investigator in Sarajevo who has spoken to the witness many times before, and the witness knows. We tried to coordinate to have that investigator present. And apparently, there's a problem. The registry says it's not possible to send an officer during that period of time that the investigator will be here. And I think the registry was suggesting a date in September when that investigator will no longer be in Bosnia. It is a five-hour drive from Sarajevo to the location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But I think this is a really serious issue, and I really would like to see whether or not there was an exchange of opinions in writing because in this Tribunal, it's unfortunately sometimes necessary to address who is responsible for the one or other issue. And when Judges have to decide it, to do so, it has to be done, and it has to be done in the framework of the time given. Probably, it may be relatively high costs caused by hearing a new statement of this witness, but compared to the additional costs for the international taxpayers when we are once again belated in this case, and taking into account what it means for an accused to be under detention, trial pending, for reasons he is not responsible for, then the only solution can be that the registry has to act and has to act immediately, even if it means that one officer has to go to this town being apparently some hours away from, say, Sarajevo. So we expect that this 92 bis statement will be taken no later than the last day of August. Any other problems in this direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: As Your Honour asked me the question, I was handed a note that the videolink witness, Witness Number 36, has contacted the OTP to tell us that the witness's spouse is very ill. The witness does not know if the witness can appear at the videolink on the 29th of July and was asking for the 1st of August. If Your Honour would like, I can double check this information at the break and see...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The 1st of August would be fine because you may know, we have the entire day. This probably facilitates this procedure. But please tell the Chamber if it's necessary as regards the other witness we discussed just recently whether it's necessary to have a Court order to the registry. No doubt, we wouldn't hesitate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So the witness may be brought in, and we go, please, into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 6.55 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th day of July, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 25
